The closest, Social, moral and ethical positions, is about identifying and evaluating a text's moral stance, and Aesthetic qualities covers language effects but not audience positioning, so a new point is the safer match.

draft.title: How a text positions its audience
card: Positioning means a text leads its audience towards a particular response, such as sympathy, doubt or approval. A reader is guided, not forced, so a different reader may respond differently.
what a text shows first sets the lens for what follows. A news story that opens with a worried resident makes readers feel for her before they hear the other side.
whose voice a text gives, and whose it leaves out, shapes whose view seems reasonable. If only the shop owner speaks, readers tend to see the problem through the owner's eyes.
words carry attitude as well as meaning. A crowd described as "a mob" feels threatening, while "a gathering" feels calm.
draft.remember: A text can lead its audience through what comes first, whose voice is heard and the words chosen.

a.q: A report on a new skate park quotes only nearby residents, who call it noisy. Which technique is mainly positioning readers to doubt the park?
opts: Giving voice to only one group
Opening with a statement from the council
Using a calm word for the park
Showing both sides in equal space
a.why: Only the residents speak, so readers see the park through their complaints. The council opening would be about order, but no council statement is described, so it does not fit.
a.clue: Ask who gets to speak in the report.

b.q: Two websites report the same protest. One calls the people "troublemakers" and the other calls them "concerned locals". What is the main way each site positions readers?
opts: Word choice that carries an attitude to the people
Opening with the most important event first
Leaving out the voices of the protesters
Repeating a point at the start of each line
b.why: The labels "troublemakers" and "concerned locals" show opposite attitudes to the same people, so word choice leads readers to different responses. The question does not say whose voices are heard or what comes first, so those options are not supported.
b.clue: Look at the labels used for the same people.

a.best: Giving voice to only one group

b.best: Word choice that carries an attitude to the people
